# Data Audit

*Generated by `scripts/run_pipeline.py`. Checks in `src/pdmodel/audit.py`; evidence tables in
`reports/tables/audit_*.csv`.*

## 1. Summary of checks

| check | result | evidence | dimension | severity |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Fully paid loans are non-defaults | PASS | Both 'Fully Paid' statuses map to 0, and over 99% of them repaid the funded principal | target definition | critical |
| Charged-off and defaulted loans are defaults | PASS | Charged Off, Default, Does not meet the credit policy. Status:Charged Off map to 1 | target definition | critical |
| Unresolved loans excluded, and rare in modelled vintages | PASS | 0.02% of 2007–2015 36-month loans unresolved (highest: 2015, 0.05%) | target definition | minor |
| Every modelled vintage observed for its full 36-month term | PASS | Snapshot Mar 2019; shortest window 39 months | target definition | critical |
| No post-origination field among the candidate features | PASS | 18 candidate features checked against 24 outcome fields | data quality | critical |
| Final model uses no post-origination field | PASS | 9 model features checked | data quality | critical |
| Samples separated in time (train/test < calibration < out-of-time) | PASS | train 2007-06–2013-12 · test 2007-06–2013-12 · calib 2014-01–2014-12 · oot 2015-01–2015-12 | data quality | critical |
| Out-of-range values below 0.1% of loans | PASS | 9 out-of-range values across 621,022 loans | data quality | minor |
| Final features at most 10% missing in training | PASS | Highest: revol_util 0.1%, inq_last_6mths 0.0% | data quality | minor |

Every check passes. The target is defined consistently, no post-origination field can reach the
model, every modelled vintage was observed for at least 39 months, and the four samples are
separated in time.

## 2. Target definition

Default = 1 if the loan was charged off (or is in default) at any point in its 36-month life,
0 if it was repaid in full. Loans whose outcome is still unknown are excluded.

| loan_status | treatment | n_loans | share |
|---|---|---|---|
| Fully Paid | non-default | 532,629 | 85.75% |
| Charged Off | default | 85,955 | 13.84% |
| Does not meet the credit policy. Status:Fully Paid | non-default | 1,789 | 0.29% |
| Does not meet the credit policy. Status:Charged Off | default | 649 | 0.10% |
| Current | unresolved (excluded) | 72 | 0.01% |
| Late (31-120 days) | unresolved (excluded) | 61 | 0.01% |
| In Grace Period | unresolved (excluded) | 9 | 0.00% |
| Late (16-30 days) | unresolved (excluded) | 5 | 0.00% |

99.6% of the 621,169 loans in the modelled vintages are either "Fully Paid" or "Charged Off". The
"Does not meet the credit policy" statuses (2,438 loans, from LendingClub's early years) follow the
same rule as the standard statuses. The 147 loans still open at the snapshot are excluded; at
0.02% of loans they cannot move the default rate.

## 3. Early repayments

| issue_year | fully_paid | repaid_3m_early_share | median_months_to_payoff | median_months_to_last_payment_defaults |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2007 | 445 | 34.2% | 36 | 15 |
| 2008 | 1,897 | 38.4% | 36 | 14 |
| 2009 | 4,558 | 47.7% | 34 | 15 |
| 2010 | 8,156 | 48.8% | 33 | 16 |
| 2011 | 12,602 | 49.4% | 33 | 16 |
| 2012 | 37,567 | 51.6% | 32 | 16 |
| 2013 | 88,044 | 57.2% | 29 | 17 |
| 2014 | 140,255 | 58.7% | 28 | 17 |
| 2015 | 240,894 | 58.2% | 29 | 16 |
| all | 534,418 | 57.2% | 29 | 16 |

57% of fully paid loans were repaid at least three months early, and the share rose from 34% for
2007 loans to 58–59% for 2014–15 loans. These loans count as non-defaults: the borrower repaid
the full principal. The target therefore measures default *before* the loan ends, whenever that
is. Because early repayment ends a loan's exposure, a vintage with more prepayment has less time
in which to default. The rise in prepayment over time would, if anything, lower recent default
rates, so it cannot explain the rising default rate seen in the calibration analysis. Defaulted
loans made their last payment after a median of 16 months.

A 36-month loan issued in December 2015 was due to finish in December 2018, and the data snapshot
is March 2019, so every modelled loan had at least 39 months to resolve. The 2016–2018 vintages
show why the cut-off matters: their resolved default rates (19.8% for 2016) are inflated because
the loans that had already finished are disproportionately early defaults.

## 5. Leakage

Every candidate feature checked against the post-origination fields listed in `config.py`
(`LEAKAGE_COLUMNS` and `OUTCOME_COLUMNS`). Outcome fields are loaded only to measure loss given
default and exposure at default, never as model inputs.

| feature | post_origination | in_final_model |
|---|---|---|
| annual_inc | no | yes |
| credit_hist_years | no | yes |
| delinq_2yrs | no |  |
| dti | no | yes |
| emp_length_yrs | no |  |
| fico | no | yes |
| home_ownership | no | yes |
| inq_last_6mths | no | yes |
| loan_amnt | no |  |
| loan_to_income | no | yes |
| mort_acc | no |  |
| open_acc | no |  |
| pub_rec | no |  |
| purpose | no | yes |
| revol_bal | no |  |
| revol_util | no | yes |
| total_acc | no |  |
| verification_status | no |  |

No candidate feature is a post-origination field. The outcome fields (`funded_amnt`,
`total_rec_prncp`, `recoveries`, `collection_recovery_fee`, `total_pymnt`, `last_pymnt_d`) are
loaded only to measure loss given default, exposure at default and prepayment. Unit tests fail if
any of them, or any other field in `LEAKAGE_COLUMNS`, is added to the feature lists. No feature
has an IV above 0.5, which would also have pointed to leakage.

## 6. Temporal validation design

|  | first_issue | last_issue | n_loans |
|---|---|---|---|
| train | 2007-06 | 2013-12 | 122,798 |
| test | 2007-06 | 2013-12 | 52,628 |
| calib | 2014-01 | 2014-12 | 162,570 |
| oot | 2015-01 | 2015-12 | 283,026 |

| Sample | Vintages | Used for |
|---|---|---|
| train | 2007–2013, random 70% | WoE bins, feature selection, coefficients, challenger fit |
| test | 2007–2013, random 30% | In-time check for overfitting |
| calib | 2014 | Fitting the PD recalibration only |
| oot | 2015–2015 | Untouched out-of-time test: final performance, confidence intervals, sensitivity, portfolio |

The train and test samples are a random split of 2007–13 loans: an in-time sample for fitting and
for checking overfitting. Chronological separation starts at the next boundary: 2014 loans are
used only to fit the recalibration, and 2015 loans only for the final test, the bootstrap,
sensitivity analysis and the portfolio. Keeping the original train/test split also keeps the
developed model identical to the one documented before this audit.

Only 9 values in 621,022 loans fall outside the plausible ranges, all of them extreme incomes,
debt-to-income ratios or utilisation rates, which the WoE end bins absorb. Missing values are rare
in the final features (at most 0.1%, for `revol_util`). `mort_acc` is 21% missing in training
because it was not recorded before 2012, and is excluded for that reason. `emp_length_yrs` is 4–7%
missing but has too little IV to be selected.

## 8. Assumptions and limitations

- Only approved loans are observed (no reject inference).
- The target is a 36-month lifetime default, not a 12-month default.
- Rare missing values get a WoE estimated from very few loans (see the sensitivity analysis in the
  validation report).
- Recoveries are recorded less completely for recent charge-offs: 25% of 2014 charge-offs show no
  recovery, against under 8% for every vintage from 2007 to 2013. This affects loss measurement, not the PD target.
